subject: Business
title: Tax-Advantaged Accounts: 401(k) and IRA
description: A fast breakdown of Tax-Advantaged Accounts: 401(k) and IRA for builders.

hook.text: Your employer matches your 401(k) contributions 50 cents per dollar. That's free money most people leave on the table.

buildup.text: 401(k) and IRA accounts let investments grow tax-free or tax-deferred, accelerating compound growth.

discovery.text: Traditional 401(k): tax deduction now, taxed at withdrawal. Roth IRA: taxed now, tax-free withdrawals in retirement.

twist.text: Not capturing the employer match is leaving free money on the table — one of the costliest financial mistakes.

climax.text: Maxing out a 401(k) for 30 years at 10% returns creates over $1 million more than the same amount in a taxable account.

punchline.text: The government offers a tax break to help you retire. Take it.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between a Traditional 401(k) and a Roth IRA?
options: Traditional offers a tax break now; Roth offers tax-free withdrawals later

details.summary: Tax-advantaged retirement accounts like 401(k)s and IRAs reduce your tax burden while building wealth. Traditional accounts defer taxes until withdrawal, while Roth accounts use after-tax contributions that grow and are withdrawn completely tax-free in retirement.
details.whyItMatters: Tax-advantaged accounts can save hundreds of thousands of dollars over a career. Failing to use employer 401(k) matches means leaving free money on the table, and choosing between traditional and Roth affects lifetime tax bills significantly.
takeaways: Traditional accounts reduce taxable income now but are taxed on withdrawal
Roth contributions are after-tax but grow and withdraw completely tax-free
Always capture the full employer 401(k) match as it is free money

faq.question: When should you choose Roth over traditional retirement accounts?
faq.answer: Choose Roth when you expect higher tax rates in retirement than today, typically when you are young and in a lower tax bracket. Choose traditional when your current tax rate is high and you expect lower income in retirement. Many financial planners recommend having both types.

faq.question: What happens to employer 401(k) matches if you leave your job?
faq.answer: Vesting schedules determine when employer matches become fully yours. Some employers vest immediately while others require three to six years. Unvested portions are forfeited when you leave. Your own contributions are always 100 percent yours regardless of tenure.
